rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 5 headers. 4 of 5 are claim-shaped: 'Plan review is a high-leverage gate' (line 29) and 'What you can test and check sets your complexity ceiling' (line 36) are load-bearing declaratives naming the mechanism, matching the rule's binding clause for law/consolidation slides; 'Five things a good plan has' (line 15) and 'Three pressures that make bad plans look good' (line 23) are catalogue entries naming their subject, the rule's own NOT-violation category. Closest call: chunk 1 'Ask plan mode what changed' (line 9) is grammatically imperative/interrogative-framed, not a claim — the shape rule 15 exists to keep exercise-only. The maintainer block (line 61, dated 2026-08-25 and re-touched 2026-08-29) documents this as deliberate: 'Header is a do-move imperative (`check_lectures §4` live-do carve-out); the prompt stays student-run (`check_lectures §6` answer-must-be-theirs carve-out...)'. check_slides §15 has no carve-out of its own naming this exact shape (only orientation/catalogue/phase-label), so this is an accept-note-backed judgment call rather than a clean rule match — same call the prior instance made, and the 2026-08-29 edit (cutting the interpretive bullet) only sharpens the imperative framing further, it does not newly introduce it. The harm §15 exists to prevent — diluting the lecture-vs-exercise mood switch so a genuine declarative-inside-an-exercise beat stops standing out — is absent here: this is a lecture with ONE imperative header for a single, explicitly-justified live-do beat, and every other header in the file is claim-shaped. Not filed as REVISE; the accept-note pre-empts it. Non-blocking: a mismatched header grammar on one slide costs polish, not comprehension — the slide is still followable — same family as rule 6.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 16 body bullets across chunks 2-5 against the three low-value classes (chunk 1 now has zero bullets, post-cut — the interpretive bullet the 2026-08-29 note removed was arguably closest to this rule's spirit, 'obvious to any Claude Code user' per maintainer line 71, and it is already gone). No doctrine restatement (each remaining bullet adds a new move or example rather than re-announcing an already-landed lens — e.g. chunk 5 line 43 'Reach without calibration is what the three pressures produce' draws a NEW causal link between two previously separate ideas rather than repeating either). No self-referential design commentary (no line tells the student it is inside a pedagogy). No aphorism kicker (no bullet closes a slide by restating its own header). Closest candidate: chunk 5 line 45, 'The ceiling is not fixed. Every check you make cheap and repeatable raises it, so building a better check buys you more than approving a bigger plan.' — reads kicker-shaped (closes the deck) but the maintainer block confirms it is deliberately load-bearing new content ('The last bullet carries the raise', line 53), not a restatement of the header. Second-closest: chunk 5 line 44, 'Push reach past what you can check and you have not delegated more. You are checking less.' — introduces a genuine new distinction (delegating vs. checking) not stated earlier, so it earns its slot too. Non-blocking: a low-value bullet wastes attention but doesn't block comprehension, same family as rule 7's non-superlative sub-items.
